newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end lower in dull trade.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed slightly lower on Monday in dull trade marked by the absence of institutions or other big players, brokers said.
"Most institutions and big investors were very quiet," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a broker at Allied Phillips Securities. "Usually on Monday we see lacklustre trade."
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share price index ended 1.2 points lower at 630.9 on turnover of 7.7 million rupees compared with Friday's turnover of 50.5 million rupees.
The only big transaction was 150,000 Pelwatte Sugar at 8.75 rupees per share.
"It was very dull," said Chaminda Perera, a broker at Jardine Fleming HNB. "The market may be sluggish for a while on a lack of local buying."

Monday's doldrums came after two active weeks as investors responded to investment incentives and tax breaks included on the calendar 1997 budget which the government presented to parliament on November 7.
